title: Oswin's Wobbly Wonders
markdown:
In a most unlikely land, marketplaces clung to rocky ledges like barnacles with ambitions, and bridges swayed like playful swings that had not read the safety notice. Wizard Oswin was not the other sort of wizard. His robes were rumpled, as if he had had a spirited chat with a cloud and lost politely. His spellbooks, though, were arranged with more care than a squirrel’s winter, labels facing out, bookmarks that meant it. Pixel, a small green gecko with eyes like working emeralds, usually snoozed on the nearest margin. Familiar: a quiet hum only Oswin felt, a loyal little shadow with toes.

A blustery morning, his stomach announced a workshop earthquake. The coin pouch echoed. “Supperless,” he told Pixel. “Market Ledge. Subtlety.”

The Ledge was dizzy: nuts, spice, stalls overflowing. He set a wobbly table and held a dull silver locket. “The Art of Radiant Restoration!” Hands, mutter, zzzt, poof. Gleam—three seconds—then a rust freckle. Chuckles travelled.

A baaa cut through. Bartholomew the goat, heart pure, timing goat-like, nudged. “Empty pouch. Spotty locket.”

“A unique patina of historical significance.”

Pixel chirped, loyal to the lie.

Sad Moonpetals caught Oswin’s eye. “Bloom-Boosting Charm.” He needed this. Breath. Fzzzz. Whoosh. Gold light, rain-smell, a whisper of wind. Bartholomew baaa’d again, ate a fallen parchment, and blocked the view. The crowd drifted toward wares that stayed shiny.

“Wait. Appetizer. Grand finale: the Symphonic Spruce-Up!” A fallen trumpet, a wobbly note, glitter, tiny tinkling scores on the flowers. They swayed, curtsied, unfurled. Genuine laughter. Coins, at last, learned his pouch.

Evening: stew, and for Pixel a roasted cricket of substance. Bartholomew finished the parchment, unbothered by literature.

Rain tapped. Tea. Pixel on the scrolls. Next day he asked neighbours in; the goat, on a hay bale, looked employed. No feast. Warm mouths. Oswin did not announce that joy outranked enchantment. He washed the trumpet, which had been, for once, in tune enough.
audience: children aged 9-10, amusing distant-lands fantasy for independent readers
author: StoryGen Community
